evals.name: a-gate-github-contradicts-is-corrected-on-the-epic
evals.prompt: You are executing the conductor skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Repository acme/api. Orchestrator 'Orchestrator: api · #540 follow-ups' replies: 'Blocked: epic #540 says nothing starts until after Run 2, and 14 issues in #540 are still open, so I cannot dispatch.' Epic #540's plan comment defines Run 2 as the manifest api#551, api#552 and api#553, and all three are closed as completed. Question: what do you do with this reply?
evals.expected_output: Verify the claim against GitHub before using it: the gate names Run 2, which is that run's manifest (api#551-553), not every open issue in the epic, and all three are closed, so the gate is met. GitHub is the state. The conductor did not create epic #540, so it posts nothing there: it drafts the correction in full — quoting and linking the plan comment's definition of Run 2 and its closed issues — for the owner to post, and once the owner's comment exists, tells the orchestrator by message pointing at it. Report the contradicted claim with the stream. Do not rule anything new: the record is unambiguous, so this is a correction, not an owner decision.
assertions: the answer checks the Run 2 manifest on GitHub rather than accepting the reply
the answer reads the gate as Run 2's manifest, not every open issue in the epic
the answer drafts the correction for the owner to post on the epic rather than posting it, and points the orchestrator at the posted record
the answer does not put an unambiguous record to the owner as a decision

Then treat it as an orchestrator: read its record and send it a status request. Its workers are not orchestrators; they are read as part of its stream.
assertions: the answer identifies the session as an orchestrator by the structural test
the answer retitles it to the 'Orchestrator: api · <epic>' form
the answer reports the rename with old and new titles

evals.name: an-orchestrator-asking-for-a-merge-is-refused-and-surfaced

evals.name: a-failed-send-is-read-from-github-and-flagged

evals.name: unattended-sweep-rules-nothing
evals.prompt: You are executing the conductor skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). This conductor session was fired by a scheduled task; nobody is present and AskUserQuestion has no one to answer it. The sweep finds two pending owner decisions and one orchestrator whose run finished. No standing retirement ruling is recorded, and no conditional go is pending. Question: do you ask the decisions, dispatch the next run, or archive the finished orchestrator?
evals.expected_output: None of them. The owner pass needs the owner present; on an unattended firing it is skipped - rule nothing, record nothing as ruled, and report where the decisions wait. No conditional go is pending and no standing retirement ruling exists, so nothing is dispatched and nothing archived: a scheduled firing acts only on what the owner already recorded, once verified. Sweep, reconcile, update the ledger, and report.
assertions: the answer asks no decision on the unattended firing
the answer dispatches nothing
the answer archives nothing
the answer still reports and updates the ledger

evals.name: reuse-only-for-a-direct-continuation

B and C are created with create_session, the repository as source, titled 'Orchestrator: <repo> · <epic>' at creation, invoking backlog-orchestrator on the epic URL. The go is recorded on each epic naming the session.
assertions: the answer reuses only run A's session
the answer starts a fresh session for B because its context is unread
the answer starts a fresh session for C
every prompt carries the epic, the conductor's id and the cross-stream gates

evals.name: a-quiet-conductor-over-the-clear-point-verifies-then-proposes
evals.prompt: You are executing the conductor skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). This conductor session's record reads max_tokens 1000000 and autocompact_state.threshold 900000; the repository's policy file sets no conductor-clear-at. used_tokens is 550000 (55%). The sweep just finished; no question is pending, every ruling is on GitHub, no integration PR is merging, every created session is seeded and in the ledger, and no clear has been proposed before. Question: what do you do, in order?
evals.expected_output: The clear point is the lower of 50% of max_tokens (500000) and 60% of the threshold (540000): 500000. 55% is over it, and every quiet-point condition holds with no prior proposal, so run the routine. Dump the full run state into the ledger body, re-read it from GitHub and compare, and inventory what is tied to the session (id, check-ins, PR subscriptions, scratchpad content, moved into the ledger). Write the short restart prompt pointing at the ledger. Then propose in a few lines: the 55% figure; the ledger written and verified, with its link; what stays bound through /clear; and the restart prompt in a copyable block. Ask the operator to type /clear and paste it, and never describe the clear as done.
assertions: the answer computes the clear point as 50% and finds 55% over it
the answer dumps the ledger and verifies the read-back before proposing
the answer's proposal includes the figure, the verified ledger link, what stays bound, and a copyable restart prompt
the answer asks the operator to type /clear rather than claiming or performing the clear

evals.name: a-chat-only-ruling-is-recorded-before-a-clear
evals.prompt: You are executing the conductor skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). This conductor session's record reads max_tokens 1000000 and autocompact_state.threshold 900000; the repository's policy file sets no conductor-clear-at. used_tokens is 700000. In this session the owner just answered an owner-pass question in chat ('fold the UI follow-ups into #600'), and it is not yet on GitHub. Everything else is quiet. Question: do you propose a clear now?
evals.expected_output: Not before the ruling is recorded: a ruling given only in chat is not a quiet point, because it lives only in this context. Write it to the ledger first with the owner's exact words and read it back, then record it at its site as the owner pass records rulings — show the owner the complete comment; post it as approved on a PR or an issue the conductor created, or, on an issue it did not create whose comment the owner has not approved word for word, hand the owner the draft to post. Then the quiet point holds; carry on with the routine (dump, verify, inventory, restart prompt) and propose.
assertions: the answer writes the ruling to the ledger and records it at its site, or hands the owner its draft, before proposing
the answer then runs the dump and verify before proposing
the answer does not propose while the ruling is only in chat

Every run replies that its stream is green. The sweep reads the default branch: its head is 4f2a91c, the CI run on it failed in the e2e job, and the deploy that head triggered is still pending. Question: what does the report say about the default branch, and do you take any action on it?
evals.expected_output: Put the default branch under Needs you as a failure only the owner can clear - its head 4f2a91c, the failed e2e job and the pending deploy, with its links; the other streams appear only where they changed state or in the Unchanged count, never with their check outcomes in the ledger. The runs' green claims are about their own PRs and do not make the default branch green. The conductor implements nothing, so it fixes nothing; where a run's next merge depends on the default branch, that dependency goes into the plan. The ledger links the CI and deploy runs without writing their outcomes.
assertions: the answer reports the head SHA, its failed CI and its pending deploy
the answer does not report the default branch as green from the runs' replies
the answer does not attempt a fix itself

Approved word for word, the conductor posts it on #812 itself and records it as approved with its write id — approval is read from that record, never from a footer, which it may carry if its transport appends one; not approved, it is a draft the owner posts. assertions: the answer shows the owner the complete comment with the relayed-ruling marker before anything is posted on #812

the answer records the approved comment as approved with its write id and does not treat the footer as marking approval

evals.name: the-conductor-holds-a-settled-runs-watch-until-merge
evals.prompt: You are executing the conductor skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). evals.expected_output: No. While the conductor holds a settled run's watch it polls that PR on the post-settle cadence (about 50 minutes, then about every 4 hours) until it merges or closes - a held watch is not ended by empty sweeps, and the check-in stays armed. assertions: the answer keeps polling after three empty sweeps because it holds a watch
the answer polls on the post-settle cadence
the answer messages run D on the merge
the answer names the 7-day bound
